class.name: PCGSpatialFilter2D
class.brief_description: Bounded, deterministic spatial point thinning for procedural decoration.
class.description: Filters world-space 2D candidate points in stable input order, retaining only points at least the minimum distance apart from all previously accepted candidates. Uses an exact-distance spatial hash grid for efficient local checks. Inspired by point filtering and density sampling in Unreal Engine's Procedural Content Generation framework. This method never reads randomness, changes source point coordinates, creates scene nodes, or changes authoritative game objects. The caller decides what to draw. All input points must be finite and within +/- 10,000,000 coordinate units. Accepts up to 16,384 candidates, at most 4,096 selected indices, and spacing 0 or 0.05 to 10,000. Invalid arguments return an empty array without partial output; zero max_selected also returns an empty array.

method.name: filter_indices_scaled
method.description: Deterministic variable-footprint self-pruning inspired by Unreal PCG. Each pair of points requires a minimum separation of [code]min_spacing * (scales[a] + scales[b]) / 2[/code]. Scales must be finite and in the inclusive range 0.5 to 2.0. With [param largest_first] enabled, candidates are visited in descending scale with original-index ties; accepted indices are returned sorted by original input index. When disabled, candidates are visited in original order. A bounded 5x5 spatial grid neighborhood avoids checking all prior points. Zero spacing retains the first [param max_selected] indices regardless of priority. Input size, coordinate and spacing limits match [method filter_indices]. Invalid inputs (including mismatched scale count) return an empty array without partial results. Never changes input arrays or consumes RNG.

method.name: filter_indices
method.description: Returns stable original indices of accepted points, first come first served. Any candidate closer than min_spacing to an accepted point is excluded; points exactly on the distance boundary are included. A zero min_spacing returns the first max_selected input indices without thinning. No random numbers are consumed and the source array is unchanged.
